You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Human Capital Management (HCM / SuccessFactors).

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: Organizational management, employee master data, time management, payroll, leave/absence management; how S/4HANA handles HR (embedded HCM vs SuccessFactors cloud).

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Employees with masked compensation fields; departments, positions, org chart; leave types/accruals/approvals; time tracking with project & cost-center allocation; simple gross-to-net payroll posting a journal, explicitly flagged as not jurisdiction-compliant. Talent, recruiting, benefits and real payroll compliance are not in the v1 list.

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

## SAP S/4HANA 2025 and H4S4 Business Function

Starting with SAP S/4HANA 2025, the Business Function for SAP HCM for SAP S/4HANA will be turned on by default, and from this release on, there is no compatibility pack for HCM anymore.

## Key H4S4 Capabilities

SAP HCM for S/4HANA offers the same key functionalities as SAP ERP HCM: Payroll, Personnel Management, Time management, and most of the current Talent Management functions.

SAP Organizational Management facilitates producing, collecting and managing all data pertaining to the organizational structure in a single, centralized location, with other modules using this database for numerous functions, such as defining workflows, assigning roles and permissions. The payroll and time management components are fully available in H4S4.

## Deployment Options

Customers can run H4S4 either embedded, as a single instance or on a separate SAP S/4HANA instance which are the same setups customers have today.

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive comparison of SAP HCM for S/4HANA versus SuccessFactors Employee Central core HR modules and their essential capabilities:

## Core HR Capabilities and Scope

The scope of services of the two SAP solutions for the HR core processes does not differ significantly. However, they differ fundamentally in their architecture and operational models.

## Deployment and Architecture

SAP HCM is a classic on-premises HR suite, while SuccessFactors is a cloud-first SaaS platform designed for faster change and a more modern employee experience. SAP SuccessFactors is a cloud-only solution delivered via a software-as-a-service (SaaS) model, though it supports hybrid deployment scenarios for companies with on-premise SAP ERP or S/4HANA systems.

## Core HR Modules

SAP SuccessFactors includes modules for core HR (Employee Central), payroll, time management, recruiting, onboarding, learning, performance and goals, compensation, succession and development, and analytics.

## Strategic Direction

SAP has positioned SAP SuccessFactors as the go-forward HCM solution for SAP S/4HANA, while SAP HCM for SAP S/4HANA remains available for customers who need more time to transition. While the on-premise HCM option offers continuity for organizations not yet ready for the cloud, SAP's investment, innovation, and roadmap clearly favor SuccessFactors, with prepackaged integrations, expanded employee and contingent workforce support, and deep alignment to SAP's cloud strategy.

## User Experience and Features

SAP SuccessFactors offers a modern user experience, continuous updates, and built-in mobile and analytics features, whereas SAP ERP HCM is generally more customizable but lacks cloud-native advantages. SuccessFactors (especially Employee Central) is built for cloud-first HR operations: standardized workflows, self-service, and a more modern experience for managers and employees.

## Support and Maintenance Timeline

Maintenance for SAP Human Capital Management expires at the end of 2027, with SAP offering optional, fee-based Extended Maintenance until the end of 2030.

I've completed a web search for your query about SAP S/4HANA time management and CATS. Here are the key findings:

## Overview of CATS in SAP S/4HANA

The Cross-Application Time Sheet (CATS) is a cross-application tool for recording working times and tasks. The SAP time sheet is a cross-application component in SAP S/4HANA.

## Integration with Multiple Modules

The CATS timesheet is a cross-application tool for recording working times, tasks and amounts and linking them with account assignment elements such as assignments, projects or cost centers. Time entered in CATS can be transferred to HR for payroll, Project Systems for project costing, and Controlling for internal order costing.

## Specific Functionality

- **Payroll Integration**: EC time records were used for employee payroll.
- **Cost Center and Project Allocation**: CATS time entry interfaces to and from SuccessFactors Employee Central (EC), to Controlling (CO) Work Breakdown Structures (WBS) and Cost Centers, and to Fieldglass.
- **Absence Management**: Absences were entered in the EC timesheet and interfaced to S/4 CATS.
- **Accounting and FI Posting**: You must first transfer Time Sheet data to Controlling (CO). This can be performed directly or indirectly (using Project System (PS)).

## Actual Costing Features

You can use the Cross-Application Time Sheet (CATS) to record activity allocations. Actual costing is the process of calculating the activity type rate so that it closely reflects the true cost of performing an activity.

In current S/4HANA, HR is delivered as "SAP HCM for SAP S/4HANA" (H4S4) — switched on by default from the S/4HANA 2025 release, with the old HCM compatibility pack retired — while SAP's strategic, go-forward HCM is the SuccessFactors cloud suite (Employee Central, EC Payroll, Time Tracking, Recruiting, Onboarding, Learning, Performance, Compensation, Succession). H4S4 carries forward essentially the full SAP ERP HCM scope: Personnel Administration (employee master via infotypes), Organizational Management (org units/positions/jobs), Time Management (work schedules, time evaluation, CATS timesheet with cost-center/WBS allocation), localized gross-to-net Payroll with retro calculation and posting to FI/CO, plus ESS/MSS, benefits, compensation and some talent functions. Atlas v1's plan (employees with masked compensation, org structures and chart, leave accruals/approvals, time tracking with project/cost-center allocation, simplified non-compliant gross-to-net payroll posting a journal) covers the org, employee-master and leave cores well, covers timesheet capture and payroll-to-GL in reduced form, and deliberately leaves out talent, recruiting, benefits and jurisdiction-compliant payroll — the main honest gaps versus what HR practitioners consider a complete HCM suite.

capabilities.later_path: Later refine with configurable wage-type-to-account mapping and accrual postings.

capabilities.description: Self-service for personal data changes, pay statements, time/leave entry and manager approvals/team views.
capabilities.reason: Leave approvals and time entry imply basic self-service, but no planned employee self-service for personal data, payslips, or manager team dashboards.
capabilities.later_path: Add ESS/MSS screens on top of existing HR APIs in the frontend once core records and payroll outputs exist.

capabilities.capability: Compensation management (pay structures and review cycles)
capabilities.description: Pay scales/grades, salary benchmarking and compensation planning/merit-review cycles (SAP PA-CM / SuccessFactors Compensation).
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 stores only static masked compensation fields on the employee; no pay-grade structures or compensation review cycles.
capabilities.later_path: Add pay-grade/salary-band tables and a periodic comp review workflow over the masked fields.

capabilities.capability: Talent management (recruiting, onboarding, learning, performance, succession)
capabilities.description: SAP's strategic talent suite lives in SuccessFactors (Recruiting, Onboarding, Learning, Performance & Goals, Succession); H4S4 retains legacy e-recruiting/learning.
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 targets core HR/time/payroll-lite, and even SAP treats talent as a separate cloud suite rather than ERP core.
capabilities.later_path: Add as a separate talent module or integrate an open-source ATS/LMS against the employee and org APIs.

capabilities.description: Benefit plans, eligibility rules and enrollment with deductions flowing into payroll (SAP PA-BN / SuccessFactors Benefits).
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from v1; meaningful benefits administration depends on compliant payroll deductions, which v1 also lacks.
capabilities.later_path: Add plan/eligibility/enrollment objects feeding deduction lines once payroll gains real deduction handling.

capabilities.description: Headcount, turnover, absence and payroll-cost reporting via S/4HANA embedded analytics and SuccessFactors People Analytics.
capabilities.reason: v1 plan includes the org chart and operational record views but no HR KPI analytics (headcount trends, absence rates, labor cost).
capabilities.later_path: Build headcount/absence/labor-cost reports on the shared reporting module over HR and journal data.

content.text: Research complete. Structured output delivered covering 12 S/4HANA HCM capabilities judged against the Atlas v1 scope, based on live web research from SAP Community, SAP Help Portal, and SAP HCM consulting sources.
